subject: MotionWorks onboarding — cost & perf tuning: batching, caching, quant, routing
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>
To: Avery Cooper <avery@motionworks.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-07-30 09:12 -0700
Subject: MotionWorks onboarding — cost & perf tuning: batching, caching, quant, routing

Hi Avery,

Great to meet you on the kickoff yesterday. Per our discussion I want to schedule a focused 45-min session next week to lock down the implementation knobs we'll use during production ramp: batching strategy, prefix/KV caching expectations, quantization profile selection, and routing policy (latency vs cost vs mixed).

Key goals for the session:
- Agree on target P95 latency for interactive flows and acceptable tail budget (MotionWorks said p95 ~200ms).
- Share traffic characteristics (avg tokens per request, concurrent reqs) so we can recommend batching windows.
- Pick a quant profile for the initial rollout (quality vs cost tradeoff).
- Define routing policy & fallback model variants for capacity-constrained periods.

I've attached a short economic matrix and our quant recommendation note to help the convo. Proposed slots: Tue 8/1 10:00-10:45am PT or Wed 8/2 2:00-2:45pm PT. Which works for you?

Action items before the call: please send a 1-paragraph note with your most common request shapes (tokens in, expected output tokens) and any strict latency SLAs we should know about.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.inference.com
Attach: motionworks_econ_matrix.xlsx, rwd_quant_recs.pdf

From: Avery Cooper <avery@motionworks.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@motionworks.com>
Date: 2028-07-30 11:04 -0700
Subject: Re: MotionWorks onboarding — cost & perf tuning: batching, caching, quant, routing

Monica,

Thanks — Wed 8/2 2:00pm PT works. Short note on our traffic:
- Primary interactive flow: avg 120 input tokens / 45 output tokens (~165 total).
- Secondary batch scoring flow: 10–100 requests bundled by our front end, usually processed every 30s; average 250 tokens per scoring request.
- Peak concurrent interactive sessions estimate: 180–250 during US work hours.
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for interactive (we can tolerate p99 at ~400ms for short ramp).

A couple quick asks we want your recommendation on ahead of the meeting:
1) Quantization — we prefer starting with a profile that trades minimal quality for cost (what do you recommend for our model family?)
2) Is prefix caching viable for our session flows (we have a lot of small re-prompts per user)?

I'll drop a short summary into the Drive folder you linked.

—Avery
Avery Cooper
Head of Product Operations, MotionWorks
avery@motionworks.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-07-31 08:46 -0700
Subject: Re: MotionWorks onboarding — cost & perf tuning: batching, caching, quant, routing

Monica/Rishi,

Reviewed Avery's notes. Quick recommendations for the call so we can be crisp:
- Batching: for interactive, recommend target batch window 5–8ms with dynamic batching up to 16 requests; this keeps p95 headroom while saving token cost. For the scoring flow, use an explicit batch API with batch size 16–32 and a 250ms flush window.
- Caching: enable prefix (KV) caching for interactive sessions with a 5-minute LRU TTL for conversational histories; aggressive TTLs hurt freshness but reduce KV misses. For scoring, use result caching keyed by request fingerprint with 24h TTL where acceptable.
- Quant profile: suggest starting with "compact-q6a" (6-bit adaptive quant) as our default — it reduces GPU memory and cuts per-token cost ~2.1x vs float16 with <1.5% quality delta on our evals. Offer a fallback profile "nearlossless-q8" for high-fidelity routes.
- Routing policy: propose a two-tier policy: latency-first for interactive flows (route to low-latency pool with compact-q6a) and cost-first for bulk scoring (route to best-cost pool, quantized to nearlossless-q8 when quality must be preserved). Include an automatic fallback to hosted small-context variant if capacity constrained.

I'll prepare a one-page decision table and bring the quant rec PDF. Monica — can you add MotionWorks' concurrency curves to the econ matrix ahead of Wed?

Vivek
VP Product | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>
To: Avery Cooper <avery@motionworks.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@motionworks.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-07-31 10:22 -0700
Subject: Re: MotionWorks onboarding — cost & perf tuning: batching, caching, quant, routing

Avery/Sam — thanks for the traffic doc. Attached is an updated mutual action plan and the economic matrix with two modeled scenarios (steady-state and ramp-week). Highlights from our side ahead of the call:
- We recommend starting the interactive route on the compact-q6a profile and enabling prefix caching (5-min TTL) with dynamic batching window of 5–8ms. That should hit p95 ~180–220ms in our benchmark runs for your avg request shape.
- For batch scoring, use an explicit batch endpoint (batch size 24, 250ms flush) routed to cost-optimized pools; expect ~2.6x cost savings vs unbatched float16.
- We'll instrument two eval prompt sets you provide — one for conversational fidelity, one for scoring precision — and run A/B against nearlossless-q8 to guard quality.

Please review the attached MAP and sign-off on the document in Drive if everything looks good. If you want us to flip any defaults (e.g., longer KV TTL or different quant baseline) we'll surface the expected unit-cost delta in the call.

Best,
Monica
Attach: mutual_action_plan.docx, motionworks_econ_matrix.xlsx, rwd_quant_recs.pdf

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@motionworks.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference.com>, Avery Cooper <avery@motionworks.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-08-02 16:05 -0700
Subject: Re: MotionWorks onboarding — cost & perf tuning: batching, caching, quant, routing

Monica — we reviewed the MAP and econ sheet with our infra team. Quick confirmations and two small asks before the rollout:
1) Confirmed: compact-q6a for interactive initial rollout, fallback nearlossless-q8 for critical endpoints.
2) Confirmed: prefix caching enabled with 5-min TTL for conversational histories. We'll toggle if we see staleness.
3) Ask: can you provide a sample Redwood config snippet for the route (batching windows, cache TTL, quant profile binding) so our infra can mirror the settings in our test environment?

If you can drop the config snippet and the decision table into the Drive folder today we'll sign the MAP and kick the integration sprint Monday.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Lee
Platform Engineer, MotionWorks
